ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=BC$, the coordinates of point $A$ are $(-7,3)$, and the coordinates of point $C$ are $(-2,0)$. What are the coordinates of point $B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $AD \perp x$-axis at point D, and $BE \perp x$-axis at point E, as shown in the figure,\\
then $\angle ADC=\angle CEB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACD+\angle CAD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACD+\angle BCE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAD=\angle BCE$,\\
In $\triangle ACD$ and $\triangle CBE$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l} \angle ADC=\angle CEB \\ \angle CAD=\angle BCE \\ AC=CB \end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ACD \cong \triangle CBE$ (AAS),\\
$\therefore AD=CE$, $DC=EB$,\\
$\because$ the coordinates of point A are $(-7, 3)$, and the coordinates of point C are $(-2, 0)$,\\
$\therefore OD=7$, $AD=3$, $OC=2$,\\
$\therefore CE=3$, $BE=OD-OC=7-2=5$,\\
$\therefore OE=CE-OC=3-2=1$,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point B are $\boxed{(1, 5)}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=BC$, the coordinates of point $A$ are $(-7,3)$, and the coordinates of point $C$ are $(-2,0)$. What are the coordinates of point $B$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $AD \perp x$-axis at point D, and $BE \perp x$-axis at point E, as shown in the figure,\\
then $\angle ADC=\angle CEB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACD+\angle CAD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACD+\angle BCE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAD=\angle BCE$,\\
In $\triangle ACD$ and $\triangle CBE$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l} \angle ADC=\angle CEB \\ \angle CAD=\angle BCE \\ AC=CB \end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ACD \cong \triangle CBE$ (AAS),\\
$\therefore AD=CE$, $DC=EB$,\\
$\because$ the coordinates of point A are $(-7, 3)$, and the coordinates of point C are $(-2, 0)$,\\
$\therefore OD=7$, $AD=3$, $OC=2$,\\
$\therefore CE=3$, $BE=OD-OC=7-2=5$,\\
$\therefore OE=CE-OC=3-2=1$,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point B are $\boxed{(1, 5)}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are coordinate axes, point C is on the x-axis and is located to the left of the origin O; point A is to the upper left of C; point B is to the upper right of C. In triangle ABC, line segment CB points from C toward the upper right. Reasoning: From the problem statement A=(-7,3), C=(-2,0), so vector CA=A-C=(-7-(-2),3-0)=(-5,3). Because ∠ACB=90° and AC=BC, vector CB should be a 90° rotation of vector CA and have the same length. Rotating (-5,3) by 90° gives two possibilities: (3,5) or (-3,-5). According to the image, B is to the upper right of C, so choose CB=(3,5). Therefore B=C+CB=(-2,0)+(3,5)=(1,5).
